translationRepairs: Let Jiangyin commandery support the Liang ruler as King of Jiangyin, keeping Liang's calendar, with chariots, banners, and regalia as before; his palaces and stipends shall be maintained in full honor."

Let Jiangyin commandery be conferred to enfeoff the Liang ruler as King of Jiangyin, keeping Liang's calendar, with chariots, banners, and regalia as before; his palaces and stipends shall be maintained in full honor."
以江陰郡奉梁主為江陰王 is an enfeoffment of the Liang ruler as king with Jiangyin commandery, not logistical support. The proposal still keeps 'support' and so does not complete the repair.
Another edict named the Liang empress dowager Grand Princess of Jiangyin and the empress consort Princess of Jiangyin.
Another edict named the Liang empress dowager Grand Consort of the State of Jiangyin and the empress consort Consort of the State of Jiangyin.
江陰國太妃 and 江陰國妃 are consort ranks of the Jiangyin princely state, not princess titles. The replacement restores that distinction.

On jimao day he sent great envoys to proclaim comfort to the four quarters, issuing sealed letters of instruction to the provinces and commanderies: "The four kings changed the age—Shang and Zhou thus answered Heaven; the Five Agents succeeded one another—Xuan and Xi thus met their destined turn.

On jimao day he sent great envoys to proclaim comfort to the four quarters, issuing sealed letters of instruction to the provinces and commanderies: "The four kings changed the age—Shang and Zhou thus answered Heaven; the Five Agents succeeded one another—Xuanyuan and Fuxi thus met their destined turn.
軒、羲 are the conventional abbreviations of Xuanyuan and Fuxi. Bare 'Xuan and Xi' does not identify them in English; expanding the names is accurate and does not invent new actors.
The former primary consort, the Qian clan, was given posthumous title Empress Zhao; the heir Ke was titled Filial and Cherishing Crown Prince.
The former primary consort, Lady Qian, was given the posthumous title Empress Zhao; the heir Ke was titled Filial and Cherishing Crown Prince.
前夫人錢氏 names the late primary consort as a woman of the Qian surname (Lady Qian), not the Qian clan as the consort.
On guiwei day Emperor Jing's tomb was styled Ruiling and Empress Zhao's Jialing, following Liang's early garden-tomb precedent.
On guiwei day Emperor Jing's tomb was styled Ruiling and Empress Zhao's tomb Jialing, following Liang's early garden-tomb precedent.
昭皇后陵曰嘉陵 names Empress Zhao's tomb Jialing. The original ellipsis can fuse Jialing into her title; adding 'tomb' restores the parallel with 景帝陵曰瑞陵.

his younger brother, the late Liang palace attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, and South Xuzhou inspector [8] Marquis Xiuxian of Wukang county, was made grand general of chariots and cavalry and minister of education and enfeoffed as King of Nankang.

his younger brother, the late Liang palace attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, and South Xuzhou inspector [8] Marquis Xiuxian of Wukang county, was posthumously made grand general of chariots and cavalry and minister of education and enfeoffed as King of Nankang.
追贈 in s0067 still governs this parallel clause, and 梁故 marks the younger brother as already deceased. 'Was made' reads as a living appointment; 'posthumously made' matches the grammar.

Scattered-cavalry palace attendant, bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of Kuaiji and ten commanderies, general who proclaims martial valor, and Kuaiji administrator Marquis Qian of Changcheng—his learning is pure and refined, his bearing grave and correct. In civil affairs he upholds ritual and music; in war he quells rebellion. With heart and stratagem he has ordered home and state alike. As territorial defender, within a month he brought order. On the frontier passes [9] his merit outdid Xiao Can and Kou Xun; marsh bandits returned to the plow; mountain lords accepted Our calendar.

Scattered-cavalry palace attendant, bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of Kuaiji and ten commanderies, general who proclaims martial valor, and Kuaiji administrator Marquis Qian of Changcheng—his learning is pure and refined, his bearing grave and correct. In civil affairs he upholds ritual and music; in war he quells rebellion. With heart and stratagem he has ordered home and state alike. As territorial defender, within a month he brought order. On the frontier passes [9] his merit outdid Xiao He and Kou Xun; marsh bandits returned to the plow; mountain lords accepted Our calendar.
功踰蕭、寇 is the stock pairing of Xiao He and Kou Xun. 'Xiao Can' is an invented given name not present in 蕭.

Xu Shipu, left guard general, became general who protects the army; Wu Mingche, South Yanzhou inspector, was promoted to general who pacifies the south; Ouyang Wei, Hengzhou inspector, was promoted to general who pacifies the south.

Xu Shipu, left guard general, became general who protects the army; Wu Mingche, South Yanzhou inspector, was promoted to general who pacifies the south; Ouyang Wei, Hengzhou inspector, was promoted to general who garrisons the south.
吳明徹進號安南將軍 and 歐陽頠進號鎮南將軍 are different titles. Rendering both as 'general who pacifies the south' collapses 安南 and 鎮南.

On jiachen day Zhang Li, general who quells the distance and Liangzhou inspector, reported that in the eighth month two years before, [11] beside a remnant hill on the border of Dantu and Lanling, tidal flood had suddenly thrown up sand over a thousand qing of rich soil fit for cultivation.

On jiachen day Zhang Li, general who quells the distance and Liangzhou inspector, reported that in the eighth month of the past yihai year, [11] beside a remnant hill on the border of Dantu and Lanling, tidal flood had suddenly thrown up sand over a thousand qing of rich soil fit for cultivation.
去乙亥歲八月 names the elapsed yihai year, not a relative 'two years before' Yongding 2. The replacement keeps the sexagenary year the text actually gives.
Jiqing, son of Xiao Zhi, the Liang Marquis of Wulin, was made successor as Prince of Jiangyin.
Jiqing, son of Xiao Zhi (Liang Marquis of Wulin), was made successor as Prince of Jiangyin.

以梁武林侯蕭諮息季卿嗣為江陰王 makes Jiqing, son of Marquis Xiao Zhi of Wulin, the successor. The comma apposition can attach the marquisate—or even the succession—to the wrong person; the parentheses fix the Chinese syntax.
Xie Zhe returned without agreement. Wang Lin asked to withdraw to the Xiang; an edict recalled the armies and halted the offensive.
Xie Zhe returned from his mission. Wang Lin asked to go back and hold the Xiang River region; an edict recalled the armies and halted the offensive.
反命 is a return-report after a mission, not a statement that talks failed. 還鎮湘川 is a request to return and garrison the Xiang, not merely to withdraw.
On yingyin day the Founder feasted his ministers in the eastern hall of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate with full orchestra, celebrating completion of the inner palace.
On jingyin day the Founder feasted his ministers in the eastern hall of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate with full orchestra, celebrating completion of the inner palace.
景寅 is the Chen taboo-avoidance writing of 丙寅 (jingyin/bingyin). Yingyin is not a reading of 景.
On jingxu day Xiong Tanlang, pacifying distance general and inspector of North Jiangzhou, was made grand mentor with staff and promoted to general who pacifies the west.

On jingxu day Xiong Tanlang, general who pacifies the distant and inspector of North Jiangzhou, was granted the right to open a staff with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Dukes and promoted to general who pacifies the west.
開府儀同三司 is the honor of opening a headquarters with ceremonial parity to the Three Dukes, not the office of grand mentor (太傅). The replacement restores that honorific.

On jiawu day Ouyang Wei, inspector of Guangzhou, reported a white dragon on the south bank south of the city, [16] tens of zhang in length and eight or nine spans around, which passed west along the city road into Heavenly Well Ridge.

On jiawu day Ouyang Wei, inspector of Guangzhou, reported a white dragon on the south bank of the Jiang in the province, [16] tens of zhang in length and eight or nine spans around, which passed west along the provincial city road into Heavenly Well Ridge.
州江南岸 is the south bank of the Jiang in the prefecture, not a bank south of the city. 歷州城西道 is the west road of the prefectural city.

We have lately sent Jiang Dezao, palace attendant, to Dongyang with Our mandate to inquire into the people's hardships with the local magistrates, and to distribute grain from the capital granaries in relief.

We have lately sent Jiang Dezao, drafter of the Central Secretariat, to Dongyang with Our mandate to inquire into the people's hardships with the local magistrates, and to distribute grain from the capital granaries in relief.
中書舍人 is a drafter of the Central Secretariat, not 侍中 'palace attendant'. The original title is a different office.
On yingyin day Funan sent envoys with tribute.
On jingyin day Funan sent envoys with tribute.
景寅 is taboo-avoidance 丙寅 and is read jingyin/bingyin, not yingyin.

An edict said: "Tanlang devoured and rebelled; his crime brooks no execution. We ordered the armies to continue the concealed attack; when he is exposed to the halter and cleaver, the penal statutes will be made clear."

An edict said: "Tanlang devoured and rebelled; even execution cannot contain his crime. We ordered the armies to continue the concealed attack; when he is exposed to the halter and cleaver, the penal statutes will be made clear."

罪不容誅 means the crime exceeds what execution can satisfy; 'brooks no execution' can be read as forbidding death. The proposal's 'bit in rebellion' is a poorer rendering of 噬逆 than the original 'devoured and rebelled'.
Once he took the throne he held the burden of chief minister to the realm; he always favored lenient rule and made cherishing the people his foundation.
When he was raised to the great foothills, he occupied the office of Aheng; he always favored lenient rule and made cherishing the people his foundation.

升大麓之日 is the Shun metaphor for receiving government, not 踐祚 'took the throne', and 阿衡 is Aheng. The proposal is right on both points, but 'raised to the charge of the great foothills' is awkward English.

Yao Cha, Chen Director of the Ministry of Personnel, said: The Founder's genius was vast and his bearing magnanimous; he met every turn without a set plan—only Han Gaozu and Cao Cao could stand beside him.
Yao Cha, Chen Director of the Ministry of Personnel, said: The Founder's genius was vast and his bearing magnanimous; he met every turn without a set plan—he was next only to Han Gaozu and Cao Cao.
蓋漢高、魏武之亞矣 ranks the Founder just below Han Gaozu and Wei Wu. 'Only they could stand beside him' reverses 亞 into equality or superiority.
Wang Sengbian lacked the gift of an Yiyin yet brooded on the wrong of the Tung Palace; Zhenyang leaned on northern troops yet never remembered Mu Ying's tears.
Wang Sengbian lacked the gift of an Yiyin yet brooded on the wrong of the Tong Palace; Zhenyang leaned on northern troops yet never remembered Mu Ying's tears.
桐宮 is Tong Palace in the Yi Yin–Tai Jia allusion. Tung is not the pinyin of 桐.
On "Renwei General, Gaozhou Inspector Huang Fahe made Grand Mentor with staff equal to the three dukes"—note:
On "Renwei General, Gaozhou Inspector Huang Fahe made Equal in Rites to the Three Dukes with the right to open a headquarters"—note:
The collation lemma is 開府儀同三司, a prestige equal-to-the-three-dukes commission, not Grand Mentor (太傅).
On "advanced to General Who Pacifies the South"—note:
On "advanced to General Who Garrisons the South"—note:
The lemma is 進號鎮南將軍. Rendering 鎮南 as 'Pacifies the South' erases the contrast with 平南將軍 in the following note.
Advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the South—comment:
Advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the South—comment:
The same lemma 鎮南將軍 was rendered as Pacifies the South in the literal field, collapsing it with 平南.
reads "General Who Pacifies the South"; the Southern Dynasties annals also read "General Who Pacifies the South"—correct.
reads "General Who Pacifies the South"; the History of the Southern Dynasties here also reads "General Who Pacifies the South"—which is correct.
《南史》 is the History of the Southern Dynasties, not a generic 'Southern Dynasties annals'. The replacement names the work.
On "jiawu day, Guangzhou Inspector Ouyang Wei reported a white dragon on the south bank": the Southern Dynasties Annals of Emperor Wu read jiazi.

On "jiawu day, Guangzhou Inspector Ouyang Wei memorialized that a white dragon was seen on the south bank of the river at the prefecture": the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties read jiazi.
The lemma has 表稱, 見于, and 州江南岸, and the witness is 《南史·陳武帝紀》. The original drops those details and misnames the History of the Southern Dynasties.
